questions.stem: When does data hosted in databases, warehouses, marts, lakes or vaults become a Data Liability?
options: When it is not utilised properly, has no proper ROI and cannot be used for revenue generation or management decision-making
When it is stored in more than one system
When it is older than the retention period
When it is used by more than one department
When it is stored in a NoSQL database
questions.explanation: Data that costs money to host but delivers no ROI, no revenue and no decision support is a liability: you pay for something and get nothing.

questions.stem: What happens when Data Liabilities overcome Data Assets in an organisation?
options: The value of data is negatively impacted
The data warehouse must be rebuilt
questions.explanation: If liabilities outweigh assets, the overall value of the organisation's data is damaged.

questions.stem: Which objective should be one of the major KPIs for any Chief Data Officer?
options: Increase the volume of stored data
Reduce data liabilities as much as possible
Move all data to object storage
questions.explanation: Reducing data liabilities as far as possible is named as a major KPI for a CDO.

questions.stem: How does poor Data Quality turn data into a liability?
options: It increases the cost of encryption
It forces the data to be re-partitioned
It prevents data from being backed up
It makes data unreadable by ETL tools
Users do not trust the data, so it is a liability to maintain
questions.explanation: If users do not trust data because of bad quality, the data is not used and becomes a liability to maintain.

questions.stem: How does a lack of Data Democratisation make data a liability?
options: It exposes data to security breaches
A non-data-friendly organisational culture means users do not use data for decision-making
It causes data to be duplicated across vendors
It prevents the creation of golden records
questions.explanation: Where the culture is not data-friendly, users do not base decisions on data, so the data being maintained becomes a liability.

questions.stem: How do missing Golden Records in Master and Reference Data contribute to Data Liabilities?
options: They lead to redundant data, and excess data is a liability to maintain
They prevent users from logging in
They increase the cost of data lineage tools
questions.explanation: Without proper master and reference data, redundant data is expected, and that excess data is a liability to maintain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a reason that Data Assets can become Data Liabilities?
questions.explanation: The reasons listed include Security and Privacy, Quality, Democratisation, Self-Service, Master and Reference Data, Metadata, Lineage, Governance and Catalog; compression is not among them.

questions.stem: Which two items are named as the biggest data liabilities?
questions.explanation: The two biggest data liabilities named are Data Swap and Dark Data.

questions.stem: According to the tagline offered for defending the ROI of data governance initiatives, how does Data Governance keep the balance between Data Assets and Data Liabilities?
questions.explanation: The tagline states that Data Governance keeps the balance between Data Assets and Data Liabilities by implementing DLP.

questions.stem: What common thread links every listed cause of Data Liabilities?
options: Each involves data underutilisation, and any underutilised data is a liability
Each involves excessive data quality checks
questions.explanation: In every case the effect is that data is underutilised in some way, and any underutilised data is a liability for the organisation.
